habit_scope: Light metal-plate roof trusses, generally 24 in o.c. (AF&PA Roof Trusses). ALT to stick rafters on a 1–2 story wood SFR. Gable ends still conventional common rafter + studs. Not floor trusses. Not SIP. Dry-in / ice is Gap. HUD 8d 6/12 sheathing folded in.
how_it_is_done: Walls plumbed and braced. Glencoe ch16: temporary wall braces stay until ceiling/roof AND exterior sheathing exist. P08 PRECEDES this method.

Shop drawings / manufacturer engineering. HUD §5.6.3: building designer gives design loads, truss profile, support locations, specials. Permanent bracing at locations designated by the truss designer or warranty void. Temporary bracing during construction is the builder's (WTCA / Metal Plate Connected Wood Truss Handbook pointed). ANSI/TPI 1 named. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.

Store on a flat, clean area (CMHC Ch11). Essential Guide: banded trusses lifted off top chords; store horizontally on blocking so plates are not loosened; peaks up (scissors different). Do not invent a blocking o.c.

Lift vertical; avoid lateral bending. CMHC: shorter than 6 m (20 ft) span usually by hand; longer need special lift. Essential: lift at balance points. Canadian lift-length is CMHC — confirm AHJ; not a crew count.

FIRST-TRUSS DISAGREEMENT — keep both; follow the truss manufacturer / TPI sheet on site. CMHC Fig 80: gable truss is placed first and braced to the ground and wall; 'Gable ends are normally sheathed prior to installation of end braces.' Essential Guide: TPI-style first truss 8–12 ft in from the end wall, then brace to the end wall; gable-end truss is difficult to brace back to the deck.

Subsequent trusses generally 24 in o.c. (CMHC 600 mm / 24 in.; AF&PA generally 24 in o.c.). CMHC: toe-nailed to the top plates. Nail SIZE to the plate: Gap (gap-P09-truss-to-plate-nail). Do not invent 16d from FM's site-built rafter-truss nails onto a metal-plate package.

Plumb and position, then permanent bracing per manufacturer (CMHC Fig 81: top-chord plane, lateral web bracing, braced bays ~6 m / 20 ft as required by manufacturer — Canadian). HUD: properly attached roof sheathing provides adequate overall bracing except long compression webs. Roof sheathing folded here: HUD §5.6.4 8d 6/12; AF&PA panel stamp for span/gap.
Do not notch, drill, cut, or alter roof trusses (CMHC Ch11). Field-cut webs are not this method.

Gable ends: AF&PA — usually framed conventional common rafter + gable studs; eave overhangs by extending top chords. Hip/valley: modified trusses or conventional framing (AF&PA; Essential hip/valley/girder truss anatomy).

Truss uplift / ceiling separation (AF&PA): gypsum may float — unattached at least 18 in from the ceiling/wall intersection when trusses are perpendicular to partitions (Fig 73). Not a skip of bracing.

Logan: truss package is an order from Burton SLC or Sunpro Lindon, not Logan will-call (MarketNote mn-logan). Not a Method. Fontana still gets a roof truss or rafter package — no Utah snow pack on that roof (mn-fontana).
Dry-in / ice is NOT this Method (gap-P09-ice-underlayment-unsourced). Logan ice barrier is the city sheet. Fontana does not get a Utah snow pack.
trades: framing subcontractors (AF&PA names subcontractors / job foreman / inspector; HUD names builder for temp brace — no crew size)
crew_notes: not in sources as a headcount; Gap gap-crew-counts. CMHC 'by hand' vs special lift is span, not people.
tools_equipment: Named: temporary braces to ground/wall (CMHC Fig 80); 2x4 web bracing as required by manufacturer (CMHC Fig 81); lift/spreader for long trusses. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Shop drawings / truss designer bracing on site (HUD §5.6.3).
Temporary bracing before the system is sheathed (CMHC Fig 80; HUD temp brace is builder's).
Do not cut or alter trusses (CMHC).
Spacing generally 24 in o.c. (AF&PA; CMHC 600 mm — Canadian / confirm AHJ).
Permanent web/lateral bracing per manufacturer (CMHC Fig 81; HUD long webs).
P08 temp wall braces still in until roof/ceiling AND exterior wall sheathing exist (Glencoe ch16).
material_classes: truss hangers / anchors CLASS (manufacturer or code — not a brand)
material_classes_notes: CLASS only. Do not shop a truss brand. Logan order plant is MarketNote, not a CLASS.
typical_duration_sfr: unknown — not in sources. CMHC 'about two weeks' framing+roofing is Canadian sequence text, not our lag table.
when_this_beats_habit: Wall-to-wall span, no interior bearing partitions, faster set (AF&PA; HUD). HUD: generally more efficient than stick; now used in many new homes. CMHC “most houses” is Canadian / confirm AHJ — not a flip of the AF&PA conventional rafter habit on this US first pass.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Field-cutting webs. Skipping manufacturer permanent brace. Treating CMHC gable-first as the only legal first-truss (Essential 8–12 ft in is the other sourced method — keep both). Copying Logan ice/snow onto Fontana. SIP roof is not this method.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did — this is the volume roof. What they skip is manufacturer brace, no-cut, and first-truss brace before anyone hangs off an unbraced gable.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Truss profile, loads, bearings, and permanent bracing on drawings. Engineer / truss designer when the package is used. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. No stamp from this KB.
risk_if_swapped_late: Truss vs stick after permit changes bearings, interior walls, hangers, and the sheathing module. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: Roof trusses 24 inches on center, engineered by the plant from your loads. Brace the first one plumb, then the rest. Leave the designer’s braces. Sheathing is still 8d at 6 and 12. Do not nail the drywall to the truss within about 18 inches of a partition. Ice felt is not in the assigned US books — Logan’s ice barrier is the city sheet. Do not put a Utah snow pack on a Fontana roof. This is the alt to stick rafters.
spanish_summary: La mayoría de casas llevan paquete de cerchas de techo, por lo general a 24 pulgadas, diseñadas en planta. Se arriostran al levantar — sin riostra la cercha no es estable. No se cortan. El forro viene después. En Logan el pedido sale de SLC o Lindon, no del will-call local. Fontana también tiene techo; no le ponga el paquete de nieve de Utah.
locators: CMHC Ch11 printed 118–121, Figs 77–81; 'do not cut or alter' printed 121 (txt ~6858–7054). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
AF&PA Roof Trusses (txt 781–794); generally 24 in o.c.; gable conventional; Fig 73 float 18 in.
HUD RSDG §5.6.1–5.6.3 (txt ~12457–12619): metal-plate 2x4/2x6; designer loads/profile/supports; permanent brace or warranty void; sheathing braces overall except long webs; ANSI/TPI 1-07.
Essential Guide: Handling and Storing Trusses; first truss 8–12 ft in from end (disagrees CMHC gable-first — keep both).
confidence_notes: Habit flag sourced in three US/Canadian books. First-truss location is a kept disagreement, not a winner. Truss-to-plate penny is Gap.
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching an existing roof, occupied-site, shoring) not in these five books — Gap, do not invent.

fastener_schedule.source: HUD RSDG §5.6.4. AF&PA silent on roof-panel pennies.

layering: Trusses unstable until braced (CMHC Ch1/Ch11; Essential). Temp brace before walk/sheathe.
Generally 24 in o.c. (AF&PA; CMHC 600 mm — Canadian).
Do not cut, notch, or drill (CMHC).
Sheathing after plumb (m-P09-roof-sheathing). HUD: sheathing is overall brace except long webs.
Gable sheathed before end braces (CMHC Fig 80 note) — keep with Essential 8–12 ft first-truss; do not pick a winner.
code_to_check: ANSI/TPI 1 (HUD names ANSI/TPI 1-07). Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
Truss manufacturer installation / bracing sheet on site. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
CMHC / NBC is Canadian — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not invent IRC R802.
No stamp from this KB. No skip-inspection.
time_money: Truss vs stick is a permit-gate layout choice (interior bearings, speed of close-in). No dollars in sources. Logan plant order is MarketNote, not a price.

Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Keep Essential 8–12 ft first-truss as the other sourced method.
